newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel rules out softening of EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Waigel rules out softening of EMU criteria.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday he would oppose a softening of the criteria for participation in the planned European monetary union (EMU).

He told a parliamentary debate that EMU participants would be decided in May 1998 and that the degree of their convergence would determine the timetable for completing currency union. "I will oppose any softening of the criteria," Waigel said.
"Not all 15 EU member states will be able to or want to fulfil the strict demands of the (Maastricht) treaty and the stability pact," Waigel said.
"The decision (about who participates) will be made at the beginning of May 1998," he said.
Waigel said it was necessary for all countries to prepare themselves in good time for the introduction of the euro in terms of legislation and public administration.
"There will be no automatic participation (in EMU)," he said.
